title: Japanese Fermented Miso Farro Salad with Edamame
summary: Centering around complex fermented flavor components, this Japanese grain salad features chewy farro tossed with a red miso, shio koji, and rice vinegar dressing. Crispy pan-fried tempeh pieces marinated in tamari and mirin add protein, while steamed edamame, pickled red radish, and shredded napa cabbage provide vibrant crunch. A touch of toasted sesame oil, grated ginger, and Yuzu juice gives the salad a bright, savory depth. The fermented elements—miso, shio koji, and tempeh—work synergistically to produce intense umami notes balanced by crisp fresh vegetables. Serve this dish cold or at room temperature as a main course salad or side for grilled proteins. The grain structure holds up remarkably well over time, making leftovers even more flavorful as farro absorbs the dressing. The fermented miso dressing coats every grain, highlighting the savory umami flavor profile of this modern Japanese dish.

steps.step: Rinse pearled farro under cold tap water in a fine mesh strainer until water runs clear.
Combine rinsed farro and dashi stock with half teaspoon sea salt in medium saucepan.
Bring stock to boil over high heat, then reduce burner flame to low and cover saucepan.
Simmer farro for twenty minutes until grains turn tender with a nutty chewy texture center.
Drain excess stock from cooked farro and spread grains on baking sheet to cool down rapidly.
Cut fermented tempeh block into small half-inch cubes on cutting board using chef knife.
Whisk tamari soy sauce, mirin, and shio koji marinade together inside shallow glass bowl.
Add tempeh cubes to marinade, tossing to coat thoroughly, and steep for fifteen minutes.
Heat neutral cooking oil in skillet over medium-high heat until hot and shimmering.
Add marinated tempeh cubes to hot skillet, reserving leftover marinade liquid for dressing.
Pan-fry tempeh for six minutes, turning cubes frequently until all sides turn deep golden brown.
Transfer crispy cooked tempeh cubes to paper towel-lined plate to drain and cool slightly.
Steam shelled edamame in small covered basket over boiling water for three minutes.
Rinse cooked edamame under ice-cold water to set bright green color, then drain dry.
Shred napa cabbage thinly into small bite-sized ribbons using sharp knife edge.
Slice japanese cucumber and red radishes into paper-thin disks using mandoline slicer.
Finely chop green onions and slice pickled ginger into delicate thin threads.
Cut nori seaweed sheet into ultra-thin julienne strips with kitchen shears for garnish.
Verify all vegetable, grain, and protein components are completely prepared for assembly.
Place cooled farro grain base into large glass salad mixing bowl to begin assembling salad.
Fold steamed green edamame into cooled farro, distributing beans evenly throughout grain base.
Keep prepared tempeh and vegetable slices separate until dressing is fully incorporated.
Add red miso paste, grated ginger, and minced garlic into small glass mixing bowl.
Whisk in unseasoned rice vinegar, fresh yuzu juice, and toasted sesame oil until smooth.
Pour in reserved tempeh marinade liquid and maple syrup, whisking emulsified dressing.
Taste fermented miso dressing and season with shichimi togarashi spice for subtle kick.
Pour three-quarters of miso dressing over farro and edamame mixture inside glass bowl.
Toss grain base thoroughly using large salad spoons until every farro grain is coated.
Add shredded napa cabbage, thin cucumber disks, and radish slices to dressed farro bowl.
Fold vegetables gently into grain salad so crisp textures remain light and fresh.
Add crispy pan-fried tempeh cubes into salad bowl right before final plating step.
Drizzle remaining fermented miso dressing over top of assembled Japanese grain salad.
Divide salad evenly among four wide chilled porcelain grain salad bowls.
Scatter toasted white sesame seeds and black sesame seeds generously across bowl tops.
Garnish each portion with chopped green onions and thin pickled ginger threads.
Top salad bowls with julienned nori seaweed strips for ocean-fresh umami aroma.
Allow salad to rest for ten minutes at room temperature so farro absorbs dressing.
Inspect salad composition to ensure balanced colors of green edamame and red radishes.
Serve with chopsticks or salad spoons for an refreshing Japanese grain meal experience.
Store remaining salad in airtight glass containers in refrigerator for up to three days.
Note that grain salad flavors deepen pleasantly overnight as fermented miso marinates farro.
Pair salad with chilled green tea or sparkling mineral water for complete healthy meal.
Present finished Japanese Fermented Miso Farro Salad with pride to dinner guests.
